raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The CT scan (Figure 1a) clearly demonstrates a hyperdense foreign body (fishbone) penetrating the esophageal wall with adjacent extraluminal air, indicating esophageal perforation. In the context of circulatory collapse and this imaging finding, pneumothorax (or hydropneumothorax) is the most likely directly observable complication resulting from the breach of the esophagus into the pleural space.
